Kumaraswamy on Thursday asserted that the definition of energy security has undergone a fundamental transformation, stating that in today's rapidly evolving global landscape, a nation's strength is determined not merely by access to energy resources but by its ability to manufacture, innovate and build resilient supply chains for the technologies that will power the future.
Delivering the keynote address at the Special Plenary Session on "Energy Security & Supply Chains" during the 7th CII International Energy Conference & Exhibition in New Delhi, the Minister outlined India's strategy to emerge as a global manufacturing hub for clean energy technologies under the leadership of Prime Minister Narendra Modi, emphasising that industrial capability and energy security are now inseparable.
"Today, under the visionary leadership of Hon'ble Prime Minister Narendra Modi, India's energy security is no longer defined solely by access to energy resources. It is increasingly determined by our ability to manufacture, innovate and build resilient supply chains for the technologies that will power the future," the Minister said.
He noted that recent geopolitical developments, supply chain disruptions and growing competition for critical minerals have reshaped global industrial priorities, making manufacturing resilience and technological capability central to national economic security.
Kumaraswamy said India is responding to these global shifts through the vision of Aatmanirbhar Bharat, building globally competitive domestic manufacturing capabilities while remaining deeply integrated with trusted international value chains.
"India should not merely become one of the world's largest consumers of clean energy technologies. India must become one of the world's leading producers of the equipment, materials and technologies that will drive the global energy transition," he said.
Highlighting the role of the Ministry of Steel and the Ministry of Heavy Industries in this transformation, the Minister said that the country's energy ambitions would be realised only through a strong manufacturing ecosystem encompassing steel, heavy engineering, batteries, transformers, power equipment, electric mobility, construction equipment and advanced industrial technologies.
Describing steel as the backbone of the clean energy transition, Kumaraswamy said every major investment in renewable energy infrastructure, from solar parks and wind turbines to transmission networks, battery manufacturing facilities, ports and green hydrogen projects depends fund

Initiatives adopted for Quality Drinking Water Supply under Jal Jeevan Mission

The Jal Jeevan Mission (JJM) – Har Ghar Jal, was launched in August 2019, in partnership with States/ UTs to make provision for potable tap water supply in adequate quantity, of prescribed quality and on regular & long-term basis to rural households. Under JJM, as per existing guidelines, Bureau of Indian Standards’ BIS:10500 standards are adopted as benchmark for quality of water being supplied through the piped water supply schemes.
At the start of the Mission, only 3.24 crore (16.72%) rural households were reported to have tap water connection in the country. As on 18.07.2026, out of 19.36 crore rural households, around 15.89 crore (82.09%) rural households have been provided tap water connection.
Under JJM, while planning water supply schemes to provide tap water supply to households, priority is given to habitations affected by chemical contaminants. States/ UTs have been advised to plan and implement piped water supply schemes based on alternative safe water sources/ bulk water transfer for the villages with water quality issues. Moreover, any water supply scheme undertaken under JJM is approved after the recommendation of Source Finding Committee of the respective State Government, to the effect that the identified water source planned under the scheme, has sufficient yield for sustaining water supply as per required norm.
Drinking Water being a State subject, the responsibility of Planning, Designing, Approval, Implementation, Operation & Maintenance of drinking water supply schemes, including those under the Jal Jeevan Mission, is vested with State/UT Governments. The Government of India supplements the efforts of the States by providing financial, policy guidance and technical assistance .
In consultation with various stakeholders 'Concise Handbook for Monitoring Water Quality of Piped Drinking Water Supply to Rural Households’ was released in December 2024 for guidance to States/UTs. This handbook recommended for a comprehensive testing of drinking water samples at various testing points such as source, treatment plant, storage and distribution points, and remedial action wherever necessary, to ensure that the water supplied to households is of prescribed quality (BIS:10500). The recommended remedial actions include the immediate closure of chemically contaminated water sources, notifying the result to the relevant authorities and affected communities, providing safe drinking water as per JJM guidelines (at least 8-10 lpcd) through a safe source or through alternate means immediately within 24 hrs till piped water supply is restored, implementing emergency treatment measures, actions such as cleaning of OHTs, check pipe line leakage, etc. within 7 days, testing all basic and area-specific chemical as well as bacteriological parameters, and, if found safe, restore water supply from a safe source in case of chemical contaminants. GOBARdhan: Turning Waste into the Engine of India's Growth
India currently meets nearly 50 per cent of its natural gas requirement through imports, making energy security a strategic priority. Recent geopolitical developments and disruptions along the Strait of Hormuz, a route that carries nearly 55 to 60 per cent of India's Liquefied Natural Gas (LNG) imports, have underscored the importance of strengthening domestic energy production. In this context, the Union Cabinet approved GOBARdhan, the National Circular Bioenergy Scheme, with a total outlay of ₹ 23,731 crore on 06 August 2026 .
Galvanizing Organic Bio-Agro Resources Dhan (GOBARdhan) was originally launched under the Swachh Bharat Mission (Grameen) in 2018 as an integral component of Solid and Liquid Waste Management (SWM), converting bio-waste - animal waste, kitchen leftovers, crop residue and market waste, into biogas and bio-slurry, thereby ensuring cleanliness in villages and improving rural lives.
Earlier, the Compressed Biogas (CBG) ecosystem was spread across four different ministries. To ensure better coordination and accelerate the sector's growth, the Government has consolidated the entire scheme under the Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas. This reform enables a unified approach to policy, implementation and sectoral development.
The Scheme will be implemented from FY 2026-27 to FY 2035-36 and will establish Compressed Biogas as a major pillar of India's future energy mix.
Through assured demand, remunerative and stable pricing, capital assistance, pipeline infrastructure, credit guarantee and technology development, GOBARdhan will be providing the strong framework to scale up India's CBG sector nationwide.

No concession or commitment on import of Ethanol for fuel blending from the United States
articles.full_content:
Recent claims in the media suggesting that India is importing and intends to import large quantities of ethanol from the United States (U.S.) for fuel blending are baseless and factually incorrect. As per the domestic policy framework, ethanol used for fuel blending under the Ethanol Blended with Petrol Programme is sourced entirely from domestic producers. There is no import of ethanol for fuel blending from the U.S.
Further, no concessions or commitments relating to the import of ethanol for fuel blending from the U.S. have been made in the India-U.S. Trade discussions. Accordingly, any suggestion of a policy change to permit large-scale imports of fuel ethanol from the U.S. is misleading. India’s fuel blending programme and ethanol procurement continues to be governed solely by India’s domestic policy requirements.

articles.full_content:
- Bio-Binder technology converts agricultural and biomass waste into an eco-friendly alternative to petroleum-based bitumen - Technology supports Atmanirbhar Bharat by reducing dependence on imported petroleum products and promoting a circular bioeconomy - CSIR-CRRI to establish a National Bio-Binder Testing Laboratory by March 2027
CSIR-Indian Institute of Petroleum (CSIR-IIP), Dehradun, in collaboration with CSIR-Central Road Research Institute (CSIR-CRRI) and CSIR-Advanced Materials and Processes Research Institute (CSIR-AMPRI), showcased Bio-Binder Technology during a technology demonstration programme aimed at accelerating the commercialization of indigenous green technologies for sustainable road infrastructure. The event brought together senior scientists, industry leaders and research collaborators to promote technology-led national development and sustainable innovation.
The programme was attended by Director, CSIR-IIP, Dr. Harender Singh Bisht; Director, CSIR-CRRI, Dr. C. Ravi Sekhar; Director, CSIR-AMPRI, Dr. Thallada Bhaskar; Dr. V. C. S. Palla and his team from CSIR-IIP; Dr. G. Bharath and his team from CSIR-CRRI; along with representatives from industry collaborating with CSIR-IIP and CSIR-CRRI for the commercial scale-up and deployment of Bio-Binder technology.

Committee deliberates on Strengthening Human–Wildlife Conflict Mitigation through Technology, Community Participation and Coordinated National Action
The Parliamentary Consultative Committee of the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change met today in New Delhi, under the Chairmanship of the Union Minister for Environment, Forest and Climate Change, Shri Bhupender Yadav. The agenda of the meeting was to deliberate on the issue of Human–Wildlife Conflict (HWC) and the measures required for strengthening prevention, mitigation and long-term coexistence between people and wildlife. Dignitaries in attendance included Union Minister of State (EFCC), Shri Kirti Vardhan Singh, along with Members of Parliament as part of the Committee, besides senior officers of the Ministry, PCCFs and Chief Wild Life Wardens of participating States.
The Committee was apprised of the follow-up action taken on the directions issued during its previous meeting held on 18.12.2025. These included consultations by States and Union Territories with Members of Parliament from conflict-affected areas. During the meeting, the Ministry highlighted that conflict patterns vary across landscapes, with human–elephant conflict being predominant in several States, while conflicts involving tigers, leopards, bears, rhinoceroses, wild boars, gaurs, primates and other species require location-specific management approaches.
The Committee was informed about the establishment of the Centre of Excellence on Human–Wildlife Conflict (CoE-HWC) at SACON, WII South Centre, Coimbatore, announced by the Prime Minister of India, during the 7 th National Board for Wildlife meeting. The Centre has been established as a national institution for scientific research, technological innovation, policy support, capacity building and community-centred approaches for effective management of human–wildlife conflict. The Committee also noted the launch of the National Human–Wildlife Conflict Portal on 10.07.2026, as a unified digital platform for recording conflict incidents, data management, knowledge sharing and decision support. Further, it was informed that the Regional Action Plan (RAP) on Elephant Conservation for South India has been approved.
Presentations were made by the States of Assam, Karnataka, Kerala, Madhya Pradesh, Uttarakhand and Uttar Pradesh , highlighting their conflict scenarios, mitigation measures, community participation initiatives, use of technology, institutional mechanisms and recommendations for strengthening national efforts. The experiences presented underscored the importance of landscape-specific planning, rapid response systems, habitat improvement, protection of wildlife corridors, scientific monitoring, early warning systems, community engagement and inter-State coordination.
The discussions emphasised that effective management of human–wildlife conflict requires an integrated approach combining ecological conservation with protection of human lives and livelihoods.

Strengthening Varanasi's Role as a Global Spiritual Destination Through Modern Connectivity
articles.full_content:
Varanasi, one of the world's oldest living cities and the spiritual capital of India, welcomes over 15 crore tourists and pilgrims every year. While this growing influx reflects the city's global significance, it has also placed tremendous pressure on its urban transport network. Congestion on key arterial roads often results in long travel times to major religious, educational and cultural landmarks, affecting both pilgrims and residents while impacting logistics and economic activity. To address these challenges, the Ministry of Road Transport & Highways (MoRTH) proposed a transformative urban mobility solution, which was approved by the Union Cabinet last month. The Cabinet has approved the development of a 46.039 km six-lane Greenfield Ganga Elevated Corridor, along with ramps, loops and an extradosed Foot Over Bridge, between NH-19 and the Varanasi Ring Road (NH-135B) in Uttar Pradesh, at a total capital cost of ₹14,447.64 crore. Conceived as a high-speed, access-controlled corridor, the project will connect NH-19, the Varanasi Ring Road, Ramnagar, Banaras Hindu University (BHU) and other key destinations, significantly decongesting the road network of Varanasi and Chandauli while strengthening Varanasi's position as a global spiritual destination.
Connecting Millions to Kashi
The project is designed to make journeys to Kashi faster, safer and more convenient for millions of pilgrims and visitors. It will dramatically improve connectivity to the Kashi Vishwanath Temple, the Ghats of Varanasi, Namo Ghat, Banaras Hindu University (BHU), Ramnagar Fort and Kashi Railway Station, ensuring easier access to the city's most important religious and cultural landmarks.
An elevated spur between BHU/Lanka and Samne Ghat will further ease congestion at the busy Lanka Junction by separating through traffic from local traffic movement. Together, these improvements will enhance the pilgrimage experience while reducing pressure on the existing city road network.
Designed for an operating speed of 80-100 kmph, the corridor is expected to reduce average travel time across the project influence area from nearly 60 minutes to about 20 minutes, a reduction of approximately 67 per cent. Travel time between NH-19 and Kashi Railway Station will also reduce from around 50 minutes to about 25 minutes, making travel significantly faster and more reliable for residents, pilgrims and tourists alike.

Building modern infrastructure in a city with over 3,000 years of history demands an approach that respects its cultural legacy. Good News for Container Train Operators as They Can Operate Across All Routes with a Single All India Licence, Improving Ease of Doing Business
articles.full_content:
Indian Railways Simplifies Licensing Framework; Reforms to Reduce Transportation Costs and Pollution, Ease Road Congestion and Benefit Industry, Particularly MSMEs s Other Reforms Include a Uniform Registration Fee of ₹25 Crore and No Renewal Fee for Extension
Indian Railways has approved modifications in the Model Concession Agreement (MCA) governing permission for operators to run container trains on the Indian Railways network. Under the approved changes, Container Train Operators (CTOs) will be permitted to run container trains on all routes across the network under a single All India license, with a uniform registration fee of Rs 25 crore, doing away with the earlier system of separate permissions and fees for different route categories. The changes will be notified through a Gazette Notification.
Single License for All Routes
As part of the approved modifications, the existing route-wise categorisation of licences will be discontinued. Subject to approval by the Ministry of Railways, Container Train Operators will be granted a Single All India Licence , enabling them to operate container trains across all routes on the Indian Railways network.
Uniform Registration Fee
The earlier system of charging different registration fees for different route categories has been done away with. Every applicant will now deposit a non refundable Uniform Registration fee of ₹25 crore to operate on all routes on the Indian Railways network.
No Fee on Extension
The approved amendments provide that the permission granted to a Container Train Operator may be extended for a further period of 20 years after expiry. This will be done by the Competent Authority to the same operator on application, subject to satisfactory performance. No extension fee will be charged for this extension or for any future extensions to the same operator.
Relief for Existing Operators
Operators already holding Category I licenses may continue under their existing category until their concession period ends. On renewal or extension under the new license, no fee will be charged to them.
Operators in Category II, III and IV may also continue in their existing categories until their concession period ends. For renewal or extension under the new license, they will pay ₹15 crore . This is the difference between the new fee of ₹25 crore and the ₹10 crore already paid. This amount is non refundable.
These operators may also choose to migrate early to the new license before completing their 20 year concession period. They will pay the same amount of ₹15 crore for early migration.
Benefits for Industry
The uniform registration fee and removal of extension fees are expected to reduce regulatory and compliance costs for operators while simplifying the approval process.

Achieved in just over two years since its launch, this milestone marks a significant acceleration compared to the 7.94 lakh rooftop solar installations recorded over the previous ten years. The PM Surya Ghar: Muft Bijli Yojana is Government of India's flagship rooftop solar scheme under the Ministry of New and Renewable Energy.

The pace of installation has increased 3.2 times over the last nine months, rising from 5,038 installations a day in October 2025 to nearly 16,328 installations a day in July 2026.

articles.full_content:
SIDBI Expands Nationwide Presence with 71 New Branches; Direct Credit Portfolio Grows 36.8% Y-oY ECLGS 5.0 Envisages ₹2.55 Lakh Crore Additional Credit With up to 100% Guarantee Coverage for Eligible MSMEs
Some major initiatives have been undertaken by Small Industries Development Bank of India (SIDBI) during the last five years to improve the flow of credit to Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs) across the country.
These include the following initiatives:
• Subsequent to Union Budget Announcement FY 2024-25, SIDBI has opened 71 new branches across India from 01.04.2024 to 29.07.2026 to expand its reach to serve major MSME clusters and provide direct credit to MSMEs.
• As on March 31, 2026, SIDBI’s direct credit outstanding portfolio stands at ₹ 51,687 crores, as against ₹ 37,781 crores as on 31 March, 2025, registering a Y-o-Y growth of 36.8%.
• The Bank also provides refinance assistance to augment resources of Primary Lending Institutions (PLIs) to increase their flow of credit to MSMEs. As on March 31, 2026, SIDBI’s refinance outstanding portfolio stands at ₹ 4,50,571 crore, as against ₹ 3,85,327 crore as on 31 March, 2025, registering a Y-o-Y growth of 16.9%.
• SIDBI has launched a product on co-lending arrangement with Non-Banking Financial Companies (NBFCs) to provide affordable credit to smaller MSMEs, especially new borrowers, as part of its effort to reach underserved/ unserved MSMEs. During FY 202526, the Bank initiated co-lending arrangements with Regional Rural Banks (RRBs) to strengthen credit delivery and broaden financial access in underserved and untapped areas.
• Prayaas Scheme has been launched by SIDBI to facilitate access to affordable credit to informal micro-entrepreneurs/ micro-enterprises (IMEs), especially women and poor.
• SIDBI has launched a GST Sahay app for ‘on tap’ invoice-based (cash flow based) small value credit to micro enterprises using trade data and digital frameworks.
The Government has introduced Emergency Credit Line Guarantee Scheme (ECLGS) 5.0 in May, 2026. Under the scheme, MSMEs are eligible for additional credit up to 20% of the peak fund-based working capital outstanding during the fourth quarter of FY 2025–26.
The scheme provides 100% guarantee coverage to Member Lending Institutions (MLIs) towards the amount in default for such additional credit facility extended to the eligible MSME borrowers. For the scheduled passenger airlines, the guarantee coverage is 90%.
However, the scheduled passenger airlines are eligible for additional credit up to 100% of the total peak credit outstanding (both fund-based and non-fund-based) during the fourth quarter of FY 2025-26. Under the scheme, additional credit flow of ₹ 2,55,000 crore is envisaged for MSMEs, non-MSMEs and scheduled passenger airlines.
This information was given by Minister of State in the Ministry of Finance Shri Pankaj Chaudhary in Rajya Sabha today.

The Indian Institute of Corporate Affairs (IICA), Shillong, under the Ministry of Corporate Affairs, in collaboration with National Law University (NLU) Meghalaya and support of the three professional institutes—ICAI (lead co-host), ICSI (support co-host), and ICMAI(support co-host)—hosted a strategic webinar for promotion of the Corporate Mitra Scheme in Meghalaya. The webinar aimed to create awareness about the Corporate Mitra Scheme and its role in developing a skilled workforce and enhancing employability among the youth of Meghalaya, as part of the ongoing Northeast awareness campaign.
The Corporate Mitra Scheme, announced in the Union Budget 2026-27, aims to empower MSMEs, primarily within Tier 2 and Tier 3 cities – thereby strengthening the business ecosystem, by establishing a network of trained and accredited Corporate Mitras. The initiative further consolidates the efforts of the Government towards a resilient, inclusive, and formalized MSME sector that drives sustainable economic growth and job creation. The initiative directly aligns with the Government of India’s vision of a Viksit Bharat @ 2047 by fostering entrepreneurship and promoting the ease of doing business. The initiative is designed to addresses critical capacity gaps by building a dedicated cadre of local paraprofessionals known as "Corporate Mitras", who will assist Micro, Small, and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs) with essential regulatory and compliance frameworks - allowing businesses to optimize growth while creating sustainable career pathways for regional youth. The “Corporate Mitra” shall function as trusted para-professionals who bridge the gap between complex regulatory compliance and commercial development, by providing accessible and affordable support services, thereby ensuring that smaller enterprises are able to navigate administrative and compliance aspects with ease.
To build this network, the government focuses on equipping young graduates with industry-relevant knowledge and practical skills, thereby transforming them into a career-ready cadre of business support professionals capable of delivering high-quality professional assistance. Consequently, the program creates new professional employment pathways while simultaneously upgrading the quality of support available to local businesses. Accredited Corporate Mitras shall be equipped with requisite skillset and competency to handle non-core operations, including financial, taxation, accounting, governance, and regulatory needs of enterprises and small businesses. Outsourcing these tedious tasks allows local enterprises to meet all necessary legal requirements with complete ease. As a result, MSME owners can confidently redirect their focus toward core business drivers like innovation, expansion, and long-term scaling.

A delegation of the All India Kisan Coordination Committee (AIKCC) met Union Minister of Agriculture and Farmers’ Welfare, and Rural Development, Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan on Tuesday and categorically stated that Ethanol is a big opportunity for the farming sector, provided its policy is farmer-centric and the correct price of the crop reaches the farmer directly. Union Agriculture Minister Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan carefully listened to all the suggestions of the farmer leaders and, while giving his guidance, assured that the Central Government will take the farmers’ views on Ethanol seriously. Shri Shivraj Singh said that farmers are like God for him and the doors of Krishi Bhavan are always open for farmers.
Farmer leaders from across the country speak openly on Ethanol at Krishi Bhavan
At Krishi Bhavan in New Delhi, a delegation of AIKCC met Union Agriculture Minister Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan. The delegation included farmer leaders from Punjab, Haryana, Maharashtra, Uttar Pradesh, Madhya Pradesh, Telangana, Tamil Nadu and other parts of the country. The main focus of the meeting remained on Ethanol, farmers’ income, MSP (minimum support price), markets and the National Agriculture Policy. However, the farmers clearly said that they are in favour of Ethanol; they only want that the real benefit of this programme reaches the farmer and not only companies or middlemen.
What farmers said in favour of Ethanol
During the meeting, the farmer leaders made their stand on Ethanol clear and said that with Ethanol, the produce of the field will not remain limited only to the mandi (market), but will reach petrol pumps and the energy market. This will create a new and strong market for farmers. When Ethanol is made from sugarcane, maize, rice and other feedstocks, farmers will get more buyers and the problem of crop spoilage or storage will reduce.
The farmers said that they are not against Ethanol but are fully in its support. However, it is necessary that proper prices of any crop, whether maize or sugarcane, reach the farmers.
